 Local View: Protect Social Security cost-of-living adjustments
 From the column: "Proposals to reduce the Social Security COLA are out of touch with the financial pressures facing people in our communities."
 Harley Schwadron/Cagle Cartoons 
 By 
 Lisa Radosevich-Craig 
 Today at 1:03 PM 
 Listen
 Share
 Share this article 
 Opinion
 Opinion 
 Advocates for ideas and draws conclusions based on the interpretation of facts and data. 
 The Trust Project
 What is this? 
 In 1972, when I was in high school and certainly not thinking about retirement, AARP fought for and won automatic, yearly Social Security cost-of-living adjustments, or COLAs. The nonprofit did this because American senior citizens need reliable protection from rising prices; and, before the law passed, increasing Social Security payments required a specific act of Congress.
 Social Security COLAs remain annually essential for the more than 1.1 million Minnesotans receiving Social Security. The amount the COLA increases each year is determined based on inflation, so seniors’ monthly Social Security checks reflect true costs of living.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Unfortunately, Washington, D.C., insiders are proposing a flat-rate COLA, which would not keep up with inflation but would significantly cut the amount of money seniors receive. This would lead to increased financial hardship for many, especially people in their 80s and 90s.
 Most of us have sticker shock when we buy groceries and gas up our cars. The newly announced 3.6% Social Security COLA would provide some relief beginning in 2027. But even with an adjustment for inflation, many older residents would continue to struggle with the cost of groceries, utilities, and healthcare.
 I’m a member of AARP Minnesota’s executive council and read about a recent AARP survey that found that most adults over age 50 say a 3.5% COLA in 2027 would not be enough to help them keep up with rising prices.
 Social Security, for most Americans, is the only source of inflation-protected retirement income. For those of us lucky enough to receive a pension, it’s typically a flat rate and not adjusted for inflation. Proposals to reduce the Social Security COLA are out of touch with the financial pressures facing people in our communities. A smaller adjustment would weaken the value of our earned Social Security payments year after year.
 I believe Congress must address Social Security’s funding challenges without cutting the money we have earned and receive each month. That responsibility extends to today’s retirees and the generations still paying into Social Security with every paycheck.
 I’m proud to be a member of AARP Minnesota and know it will never stop fighting to protect and strengthen Social Security.
 Please contact Congress and tell federal representatives “no” to Social Security cuts.

 Lisa Radosevich-Craig of Duluth is a member of the executive council for
